title: Microtrace Collage & Filter Palette — compact request drill-down prototype
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Engineers using Redwood Console need a fast way to triage high-cardinality sessions (hundreds of spans) without losing correlation context or overwhelming the UI. Current waterfall and full-span detail modes are valuable, but slow to scan and heavy for exploratory work.

Goal: Design a compact, scannable "microtrace collage" view for request drill-down that surfaces: critical spans (latency outliers, errors), correlation IDs, timeline density, and an always-available filter palette. The prototype should support quick span comparisons, pinning spans for side-by-side inspection, and progressive disclosure into the full trace/callstack.

Scope: Console trace drill-down page; timeline strip + collage rows; filter palette (by service, span name, tag, error level, correlation id); compact hovercards with KV preview and link-through to full span canvas. Focus on layout/interaction, keyboard navigation, and transition animations (collapse -> full waterfall). Not in scope: backend instrumentation changes, new span sampling logic, or new trace storage schemas.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype in Figma clickable for desktop with timeline + collage + filter palette
Microtrace collage shows top 10 spans by self-time and marks errors and tail-latency spans
Filter palette allows multi-select and updates collage in <100ms in mock playback scenarios
Pinning workflow: user can pin up to 3 spans and open side-by-side comparison panel
Accessible: Keyboard focus for filter palette, collapsible sections with aria labels
decisions: Use a horizontal density timeline (sparkline) instead of rendering full spans for overview to improve scanability.
Highlight spans chosen by 'composite score' (self-time * error-weight) for collage rows to surface meaningful candidates.
Pinning limited to 3 spans to keep side-by-side comparison usable; allow 'persist pin' to route to full waterfall on demand.

Current implementation hits 45 fps on baseline; engineering to optimize virtualization and canvas batching. See PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4578
